All done. Here's a summary of what was built.

## Final result

**Compiled ✓ | Correctness ✓ (5/5)** | Runtime ~200–240 μs vs cuDNN ref ~14–47 μs

The kernel at [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p63/round0/output_model_new.py) implements a shared-memory tiled 2D convolution in AveLang DSL.

**Architecture:**
- **16×16 spatial output tile** per block, with all 128 output channels handled by a single block
- **Shared memory**: cooperatively loads `(18,18,16)` input window + `(128,16,3,3)` weight into ~47 KB LDS
- **256 threads** (16×16), each computing all 128 output channels at its spatial position
- **BF16** data with **FP32** accumulation throughout the inner MAC loop
- Grid: `(64, 64, N)` = 65,536 blocks for the full `(16,128,1022,1022)` output

**What I explored during optimization:**

| Version | Runtime | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Naive global-memory | 1040 μs | No shared mem, one block per output channel |
| 16×16, TILE_OC=16 | 367 μs | Shared memory, 524K blocks |
| 16×16, TILE_OC=64 | 352 μs | More work per block, 131K blocks |
| 16×16, all 128 ch | 229 μs | All channels in one block, 65K blocks |
| Inverted loop (128 accum) | 414 μs | Register pressure from `al.make_local((128,), f32)` |
| 32×32, TILE_OC=16 | crash | HIP launch failure (shared mem + 1024 threads) |
| 16×32, all 128 ch | crash | HIP launch failure (56 KB + 512 threads) |

The main remaining gap to cuDNN is the lack of Winograd transforms (cuDNN uses F(4×4,3×3) for ~2.25× MAC reduction) and MFMA matrix instructions. Integrating MFMA would require restructuring the kernel as an im2col+GEMM with warp-level tile distribution — feasible but substantially more involved.
